description: '''Anti-folk''' (sometimes spelled '''antifolk''') is a [[music genre|genre]] of [[folk music]] that emerged in the 1980s in New York City. It was founded by singer-songwriter [[Lach (musician)|Lach]], as a response to the prevailing folk music scene. It is characterized by its amateur sound, [[do it yourself|DIY ethos]], and often humorous, rebellious, or satirical lyrics. Antifolk music was made to diverge from, and sometimes mock, the perceived seriousness of the era's mainstream music scene, while often still being [[protest song|protest music]] aimed at social change. The latter element especially overlaps with [[folk punk]].
